# The hub's Playwright specs that consumer-ci.yml's `hub-browser` job runs against
# THIS engine tree (path gem), one hub-relative path per line. `#` starts a comment.
#
# WHY A SUBSET, AND WHY THESE. Engine PR #485 (engine-scripts-become-modules) loaded
# studio/studio_confetti by URL, whose Link modulepreload header resolved the bare
# "canvas-confetti" import before the import map existed. Every Rails suite stayed
# green; the hub's browser suite went red on 41 tests in 23 files ("Failed to resolve
# module specifier", hub ci run 40463820951) only after the release lock bump. These
# are specs that assert zero page errors on engine-rendered chrome across the hub's
# layouts (boards, /dreams, the devops countdown, the navbar, model pages, public
# pages), chosen so most of them went red on that regression, all of them exist on
# the hub's main, release AND accepted, and the whole set runs in about 75s.
#
# The full hub suite stays the hub's own job (its ci.yml `playwright` lane, three
# shards, ~8 min each): running it here would make every hub flake an engine red.
#
# THE HUB OWNS THESE FILES, THIS LIST NAMES THEM. A renamed or deleted spec fails the
# job at "Resolve the hub spec subset" by name rather than quietly shrinking the set;
# repoint or drop the line here. bin/hub-e2e-subset audits the run's JSON receipt, so
# a listed file that ran no test (all skipped, all quarantined) is red too. On any red
# the job's "E2E_LANE triage line" step prints one line naming the specs at fault.
# Guard: test/lib/consumer_ci_hub_browser_test.rb.

e2e/depth_chart_board.spec.js
